items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the private housing finance law, in relation to the mobile and
manufactured home replacement program
items.lawCode: Add Art 27-A §§1240 - 1242, Priv Hous Fin L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S3141

SPONSOR: MANNION
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the private housing finance law, in relation to the
mobile and manufactured home replacement program

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to establish the mobile and manufactured
home replacement program.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill would amend the Private Housing Finance law by
establishing the Mobile and Manufactured Home Replacement program.

Section 2 of this bill provides that the effective date shall take
effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Mobile and manufactured homes provide an important source of affordable
housing throughout the State. Many of these homes are older and dilapi-
dated with rusted, leaking metal roofs, holes in flooring, leaky metal-
framed windows with interior take-out storms.  No matter the amount of
rehabilitation investment, the end result is unsatisfactory in terms of
longevity, energy efficiency and affordability.

The Mobile and Manufactured Home Replacement Program will fund the
replacement of older, dilapidated mobile and manufactured homes that are
sited on land owned by the homeowner, with new affordable and energy
efficient manufactured, modular or site-built homes. This program will
have a multiplier effect for the area as local contractors, labor and
building materials are used. Eligible units of local government, or
not-for-profit organizations may apply to the New York State Housing
Trust Fund Corporation to administer a local Mobile and Manufactured
Home Replacement Program of up to $750,000.  Local program administra-
tors would be entitled to an administrative fee of 7.5%.

Eligible property owners, with a total household income not to exceed
eighty percent of area median income, may apply through a local program
for funding of up to $125,000 for replacement of their dilapidated
mobile or manufactured home. As a condition of eligibility, property
owners may not have liens on the land after closing the grant other than
the new home financing and currently existing mortgage or mortgages, and
all property taxes and insurances must be current. Recipients must live
in the replaced home for ten years, or recapture terms would apply.
Eligible property owners must complete a homeownership training program
for which includes household budgeting, home maintenance, predatory
lending and post-purchase counseling. This program is an important
component of replenishing the affordable housing stock in New York
State.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2021-22: S.6866-A (Mannion) Referred to Housing, Construction, and
Community Development.
 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

This program would be funded subject to annual appropriations made
through the State budget.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the private housing finance law, in relation to the

PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to establish the mobile and manufactured
home replacement program.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill would amend the Private Housing Finance Law by
establishing the Mobile and Manufactured Home Replacement program.

Section 2 of this bill provides that the effective date shall take
effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Mobile and manufactured homes provide an important source of affordable
housing throughout the State. Many of these homes are older and dilapi-
dated with rusted, leaking metal roofs, holes in flooring, leaky metal-
framed windows with interior take-out storm shutters.  No matter the
amount of rehabilitation investment, the end result is unsatisfactory in
terms of longevity, energy efficiency and affordability. Ultimately, it
is the mobile and manufactured homeowner who suffers.

The Mobile and Manufactured Home Replacement Program will fund the
replacement of older, dilapidated mobile and manufactured homes that are
sited on land owned by the homeowner, with new affordable and energy
efficient manufactured, modular or site-built homes. This program will
have a multiplier effect for the area as local contractors, labor, and

not-for-profit organizations may apply to the New York State Housing
Trust Fund Corporation to administer a local Mobile and Manufactured
Home Replacement Program of up to $750,000.  Local program administra-
tors would be entitled to an administrative fee of 10%.

Eligible property owners, with a total household income not to exceed
eighty percent of area median income, may apply through a local program
for funding of up to $200,000 for replacement of their dilapidated
mobile or manufactured home. As a condition of eligibility, property
owners may not have liens on the land after closing the grant other than
the new home financing and currently existing mortgage or mortgages, and
all property taxes and insurances must be current. Recipients must live
in the replaced home for ten years, or recapture terms would apply.
Eligible property owners must complete a homeownership training program
for which includes household budgeting, home maintenance, predatory
lending and post-purchase counseling. This program is an important
component of replenishing the affordable housing stock in New York
State.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:


2021-22: S.6866-A (Mannion) Referred to Housing, Construction, and
Community Development.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

This program would be funded subject to annual appropriations made
through the State budget.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 131
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 3141-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the private housing finance law, in relation to the
      mobile and manufactured home replacement program"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This  bill  would  create  a  mobile and manufactured home replacement
program that would provide local governments and  nonprofits  grants  to
operate programs to fund the replacement of dilapidated mobile and manu-
factured homes.
 
  New  York  is  in the midst of a severe housing shortage and I support
efforts to expand access to affordable homes. That is why my $5 billion,
5-year housing plan to create and preserve 100,000 units across New York
State already funds a mobile and manufactured home replacement  program.
However,  implementing  this bill would impose a significant cost to the
State, costs which are not accounted for in  our  financial  plan.  This
proposal would be more appropriately considered in the context of budget
negotiations next year.
 
  Therefore, I am constrained to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                       (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                               __________
